column1: # Hexplain Expression Language (HEL 1.0) conformance vectors.
# Each row is an expression, the context it is evaluated against, and what it must produce:
# a value, or an error whose diagnostic contains the given text (compared case-insensitively).
# A second implementation of HEL can run these; this one runs them on both its compiled and
# its interpreted path, so the two cannot agree with each other while disagreeing with the
# specification.
# Columns (tab-separated): name, expression, expectation (value|error), expected (a JSON
# literal; for an error, a JSON string the diagnostic must contain), and the context as
# standard base64 of JSON. The context is the CURRENT STRUCT (instance): its keys are the
# fields the struct declares, so a bare name resolves against it. A key present with the
# value null is a declared optional field that is absent (it reads as Null); a name that is
# not a key is UNDECLARED and must raise an undefined-name error. A runner therefore passes
# the context's key set as the struct's declared schema. JSON whole numbers are Integers and
# numbers with a fraction are Floats, so an integral Float cannot be written as an expected
# value; the rows avoid needing one.
# NaN has no JSON spelling, so NaN rows build it in the expression: 1e308 * 10.0 overflows to
# Infinity, and Infinity - Infinity is NaN.
# NOT COVERED HERE, because this format carries only a data context: eof() and stream.* need
# a stream position, evaluationInstant() needs a reference instant, inRegister()
# needs a register provider, partExtension() and asset.* need an asset, and sizeof() of a
# sibling field needs the byte spans of a real parse. Forward references need a declaration
# ORDER and a parse position, which a flat context does not have. Bytes values (and so the
# Bytes-vs-String comparison rules) and uint64 values above 2^63-1 have no JSON spelling that
# survives the runner's conversion (a JSON number becomes a signed 64-bit Integer), so they
# are not covered either; the literal-range rows cover the part of the uint64 rule that a
# literal can reach. Load-time rejection of an unsupported extension group is a property of
# a processor, not of one expression. An undefined name AFTER the first path step (hdr.typo)
# needs a nested struct's declared field set, and a JSON object in the context is read as an
# undeclared map, so it is not covered either. Those are exercised by the engine suites; the
# gap is stated here rather than left to be inferred from absence. The processor conformance
# suite (specification/conformance/, the physical-parser cases named pp-hel-*) carries them: its
# cases have a declaration order, nested schemas, Bytes and uint64 values, stream positions and
# asset contexts.
